# Verity Mod for Minecraft Guide Full Context

VerityModChecker.online helps Minecraft players find the current Verity Mod download route without using a random mirror. The site focuses on current public project status, Java versus Bedrock separation, MCPE setup, Verity Pack and VERITY.exe modpack confusion, Falsity and Verity/Falsity route separation, AI model setup, voice troubleshooting, and 404 or taken-down links.

The homepage explains that Verity Mod refers to separate Minecraft Java and Bedrock community projects based on the Verity AI horror character, then presents a current file map checked July 29, 2026. It links directly to exact maintainer release records, identifies owners, Project IDs, filenames, file sizes, publication dates, and point-in-time project reach. At this check, the CurseForge totals for Verity JE, Verity BE, PnTMC, and Verity Pocket Edition (Be) are 2,339,762, 4,024,803, 7,340,670, and 56,652 downloads; the official Verity JE Modrinth project total is 332,321. The same facts are available as machine-readable JSON and an Atom update feed. The source and file checker reviews URLs, project paths, Project IDs, release record numbers, filenames, package extensions, and displayed file sizes. It calculates local SHA-256 fingerprints without uploading a selected file and compares recognized Java JAR hashes with Modrinth's published SHA-512 values. The route chooser separates Java beta, Java stable, Fabric-loader checks, the exact Verity BE route, broader Bedrock comparisons, and MCPE setup questions.

It exists because the XML sitemap lists URLs but does not explain which page answers Java downloads, Bedrock imports, MCPE setup, APK claims, VERITY.exe modpacks, Verity Pack confusion, Falsity Mod confusion, play steps, server setup, voice problems, Groq and OpenRouter errors, status 401, status 429, lag, no-response symptoms, map rumors, creator citations, JSON data, or update-feed intent. A modpack is a profile route and should not be treated as the same artifact as a standalone Java jar. The dedicated Pocket Edition page compares Verity BE, PnTMC, and Verity Pocket Edition (Be), then explains why APK, EXE, password ZIP, and Java JAR routes do not answer normal MCPE install intent.

The APK and app safety page targets mobile searches where users type "Verity Mod APK," "Verity Mod for Minecraft PE app," or similar Google Play-style wording. It explains that APK files install Android apps while normal MCPE add-on routes use `.mcaddon` or `.mcpack` packages. It compares app claims against Verity BE record `8506198`, PnTMC record `8517480`, Verity Pocket Edition (Be) record `8406293`, and MCPEDL route notes; it also teaches users to check publisher identity, store disclosures, permissions, ads, final host, and whether a maintainer project page links to the app before treating it as official. As of July 27, 2026, current Play Store examples on the page include BirchApps package `com.verity.stalker.mobs.birchappsmcpe`, GO:KU STUDIO package `com.goku.verity.horror`, L13DEVSTUDIO package `com.l13devstudio.verit`, Real Games Villa package `verity.mod.minecraft.pemodverity`, and richard7 package `com.richmcpe.verity`, all framed as third-party app claims rather than maintainer MCADDON replacements. The same app-claim facts are available as machine-readable JSON at `/data/verity-app-claims.json`.

It also explains why search results or lower MCPEDL download rows can still show previous PnTMC records `8503821`, `8327253`, `8327250`, or `8327242`: they remain older Bedrock files, not Java routes or separate projects. MCPEDL displays V26.30, V26.20, and V26.10 package choices, so players should match their Bedrock build instead of importing a Java JAR or a random mirrored APK, EXE, or password ZIP. The route now also points no-reply and no-monster-form complaints to the PnTMC wake phrase, distance, pack activation, clean-world, trigger, and feature-expectation checks.

The commands page at `/commands/` targets "Verity Mod commands," "verity command," "minecraft verity command," `/script debugger connect`, `/verity_language`, "Hey Verity," `/verity give_ball`, `/verity event prophecy`, `/verity event anomaly`, `/verity status`, and current tutorial-video command searches. The AI model page compares Groq, supported OpenRouter configurations, and local Ollama. The page does not collect keys. It warns players not to paste API keys into download pages, Reddit, Discord, or random forms. It also separates text response problems from voice output problems.

The Verity Mod Groq API key setup page at `/verity-groq-api-key/` is the exact credential-intent route for searches around "Verity Mod Groq API key," "Groq API key," "Grok API key," "Verity API key," OpenRouter credentials, Ollama setup, 401, 403, 429, blank replies, and no-response symptoms after the Java mod loads. It tells players to confirm the Verity JE Java route first, create keys only inside the official provider dashboard, keep keys local, distinguish Groq from OpenRouter, treat Ollama as a local service route, test one short typed prompt before voice, and avoid replacing the Verity Mod file for provider status codes. Aliases such as `/groq-api-key/`, `/grok-api-key/`, `/verity-api-key/`, `/verity-grok-api-key/`, `/verity-openrouter-api-key/`, and `/openrouter-api-key/` redirect to this canonical guide.

The API connection failed page maps status 401, 403, 404, 429, provider 5xx responses, and local Ollama connection failures to the correct layer. It includes a no-key quick diagnosis selector for provider plus symptom, covering Groq, OpenRouter, Ollama, unknown providers, null or blank replies, and text-working-but-voice-failing cases. It also answers the high-intent API-key question: Groq keys come from Groq Console, OpenRouter keys come from OpenRouter, and Ollama normally needs a local running service rather than a cloud API key. It explains that a provider status code normally appears after the Java mod has loaded, so players should not replace the jar to fix a rate limit, and that a change from 401 to 429 can mean authentication now works but quota is limiting the account. It links to the current Verity JE project, maintainer tutorial, and primary Groq, OpenRouter, and Ollama documentation.

The status-401 page targets exact Verity Mod API connection failed 401 intent from Search Console and public player troubleshooting. It treats 401 as a credential and provider-mismatch page rather than a generic download page: Groq, OpenRouter, Ollama, and unknown routes are separated, the page explains missing keys, revoked keys, copied spaces or quotes, wrong-provider keys, wrong config fields, and exposed-key rotation, and it tells players to restart once and test one short typed prompt before changing the jar, model, voice setup, or provider. Aliases such as `/401/`, `/verity-mod-401/`, `/api-401/`, `/api-connection-failed-401/`, `/verity-api-connection-failed-401/`, `/verity-error-401/`, `/verity-groq-401/`, and `/groq-401/` redirect to this canonical guide.

The status-429 page targets the exact "Verity Mod status 429" intent visible in Search Console and current player discussions. It treats 429 as a provider rate-limit page rather than a generic download page: Groq, OpenRouter, and local Ollama routes are separated, the page explains why Verity can work briefly and then fail again, why another API key may share the same account or organization ceiling, and why the safe retest is one short text prompt after the provider reset window. It links back to the broader API connection guide, AI model page, voice page, and current Verity JE route.

The how-to-talk page separates four current interaction routes and now targets exact "how to talk to Verity Mod" and microphone searches. Verity JE needs a working AI provider before text and voice testing. Verity BE tells players to type Verity before a message and documents its Beta API and backend requirements. The separate PnTMC Bedrock project documents chat while Verity is on the ground, the Hey Verity inventory wake phrase, and a distance rule. VERITY.exe is handled as a modpack route where direct chat, voice chat, Groq/API key, microphone permission, and provider quota must be tested separately. The page now covers players who say Verity does not reply, microphone input does not work, voice chat does not trigger, or Verity never transforms into the expected monster form: first prove the route, text response, clean world/profile, nearby state, active packs, and documented trigger expectations instead of swapping to a mirror. The page does not combine instructions across projects.

The Verity doesn't respond page at `/verity-doesnt-respond/` is the exact symptom route for "Verity Mod doesn't respond," "Verity not responding," "Verity no reply," "Verity doesn't talk," dots-only, silent voice, Pocket Edition daily-limit, and missing monster-form searches. It tells players to test typed text before voice and to debug by layer: Java AI provider or local Ollama, Bedrock pack and world settings, Verity BE backend/setup, Verity Pocket Edition online AI and Cloudflare Workers limit notes, PnTMC ground chat or Hey Verity wake phrase, MCPE package imports, and modpack assumptions. Aliases such as `/verity-mod-doesnt-respond/`, `/verity-not-responding/`, `/verity-ai-not-responding/`, `/verity-no-reply/`, `/verity-doesnt-talk/`, `/verity-pocket-edition-daily-limit/`, `/verity-cloudflare-workers-limit/`, and `/verity-only-says-dots/` redirect to this route.

The not-working, voice-not-working, and taken-down pages handle symptom searches: crashes, old links, 404 pages, unsafe mirrors, box not spawning, dialogue missing, Error: No Purpose, only saying "...", chat works but voice is silent, and suspected unsafe reposts. The not-working hub links Error: No Purpose users to the dedicated Verity BE page rather than making them guess between Java API, Bedrock setup, PnTMC, and mirror-download fixes.
